Perceived main threats to the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force's mission to safeguard maritime interests: territorial disputes with China and South Korea (East China Sea/South China Sea islands), North Korea's nuclear and missile programs threatening maritime trade, and natural disasters (earthquakes/tsunamis) affecting maritime infrastructure. #japan #maritime-security

Japan addresses maritime threats via modernizing navy capabilities, strengthening alliances (esp. US), boosting maritime surveillance/defense, more joint exercises, and a comprehensive maritime security strategy. #japan #maritime-security

Japan's naval modernization examples: advanced maritime surveillance network plus UAVs and maritime patrol aircraft; anti-submarine warfare (new sonar, aircraft, submarines) to counter North Korea's submarine fleet; amphibious assault capability (new amphibious force, amphibious vehicles and aircraft) to defend remote East China Sea islands; ballistic missile defense with Aegis destroyers and PAC-3; and a cyber defense unit for naval assets. #japan #maritime-security #navy-modernization

Japan's most important ally is the United States, via the US-Japan security alliance (US forces stationed in Japan, tech access, intelligence sharing, deterrence). Japan also has security partnerships with Australia, Canada, and ASEAN members, plus the Quad (US, India, Australia, Japan). #japan #alliances

Japan's current maritime security strategy, first announced in 2013, has three key components: (1) active contribution to peace, (2) protecting territorial integrity and territorial waters, (3) promoting an open and stable rules-based maritime order. #japan #maritime-security

Japan's maritime strategy evolved from Cold War defense against the Soviet Union, to 1990s emphasis on regional cooperation (China, South Korea, ASEAN Regional Forum, US alliance), to the 2013 three-pillar strategy balancing deterrence and diplomacy. #japan #maritime-security

Joint exercises Japan participates in: RIMPAC (US-hosted, biennial), Cope North (US/Japan/Australia, air ops), Keen Sword (biennial US-Japan ground/naval/air), Blue Flag (Israel-hosted air exercise), and Malabar (US/Japan/India naval). #japan #exercises

Japan's territorial disputes with China (Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands) and South Korea (Takeshima/Dokdo Islands) drive its maritime security strategy: strengthening capabilities and deepening ties with the US, Australia, India, and ASEAN, while pursuing diplomacy with China and South Korea. #japan #maritime-security

Japan promotes regional peace via economic development: Partnership for Quality Infrastructure (port development), the Asian Development Bank, the Greater Mekong Subregion Economic Cooperation Program, and pushing the Japan-China-South Korea Free Trade Agreement. #japan #economic-development

cluster1 (GKE1) stores secrets as Kubernetes Secrets managed by SOPS; GKE2 is intended to consume secrets via the Google Secret Manager API instead of Kubernetes Secrets. #sops-gke-migration #gke #sops

SOPS-managed secrets in user's clusters are identified by the annotation `sops.k8s.pgp.mozilla.org/encrypted: "true"`; filter with `kubectl get secrets -n <ns> -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations."sops.k8s.pgp.mozilla.org/encrypted" == "true") | .metadata.name'`. #sops-gke-migration #sops

Migration procedure established for user: export secret with kubectl -o yaml, decrypt with `sops -d`, then `gcloud secrets create <name> --replication-policy="automatic"` and `gcloud secrets versions add <name> --data-file=...`. User works on / is interested in single-image rain removal (deraining) research and asked how to download the Rain100L and Rain100H benchmark datasets. #rain100 #deraining #datasets

Rain100L and Rain100H both come from the joint rain detection and removal project page at http://www.icst.pku.edu.cn/struct/Projects/joint_rain_removal.html (Yang et al., "Deep Joint Rain Detection and Removal from a Single Image"). Downloads are Rain100L.zip and Rain100H.zip, each extracted into rainy_image/ and ground_truth/ folders. #rain100 #deraining #datasets

Rain100L vs Rain100H: the difference is rain density/strength, not image resolution — "L" = light rain streaks, "H" = heavy rain streaks. Both are 100-image-pair test sets (from a larger 1800-pair training pool). #rain100 #deraining

Correction: an earlier answer in this chat wrongly described Rain100H vs Rain100L as differing in image quality/resolution (claiming H is 720p+ and L is 400x400). That is inaccurate — both sets are 100 pairs; the distinction is heavy vs light rain streaks. #rain100 #deraining
